messages:
Priya R.: heads up — ACME reported a spike in API latency starting ~02:10 UTC. p50 ~120ms -> 300ms, p99 up to 900ms. They say requests from us-west are hitting ap-southeast. Can we triage?
Jason K.: saw alert from support-bot as well. any trace IDs/req ids?
support-bot: alert: notify support@acme - high_latency spikes - trace_id=trc_01F23X - sample_rate=1%
Priya R.: trace_id trc_01F23X attached to their support ticket. I pulled the span list — origin ip geo is us-west but server endpoint resolved in ap-southeast1.
Erin L.: can you paste the full trace context? any LB logs?
Priya R.: snippet: 
```
span: req_start us-west1 -> dns -> resolved ap-southeast1
route: client -> nginx-edge-us -> envoy-proxy -> ap-southeast1:443
latency: dns 12ms, connect 280ms, tls 310ms
```
Maya S.: that's consistent with a routing rule fallback. we had a canary rule for mesh egress yesterday. I will check canary flags.
Dave (SRE): running a quick traceroute from our synthetic runner in us-west to the model endpoint now.
Dave (SRE): `traceroute -n model.redwood.ai` -> shows first hops local, then next hop ASN 7545 (apac peer) at hop 6, RTT 220ms.
Jason K.: I deployed a tiny health-check change at 02:04 UTC to the regional balancer config (rolling). Could that have flipped health states? I didn't touch peering but did change timeout from 2s -> 1s.
Maya S.: ah — shortened health timeout could cause transient flaps; LB may mark us-west as unhealthy and route to remote region via cross-region peering. checking LB health events...
infra-bot: LB event: us-west1 pool marked UNHEALTHY at 02:07:21 by probe-timeout, restarted check; 02:09:40 pool still UNHEALTHY, fallback policy->route_to_nearest_backup=true
Priya R.: acme reported first bad call 02:10:18 — matches.
Erin L.: can we reproduce locally? Steps: 1) set health probe timeout 1s 2) cause slow startup on us-west backend 3) make requests from us-west synthetic. That should force failover to backup region.
Dave (SRE): repro successful in staging. Showed routing to ap-southeast with +250ms.
Maya S.: immediate remediation: revert health timeout to 2s on production balancer. I'll patch now and monitor.
Maya S.: reverted at 02:32 UTC. infra-bot: LB event: us-west1 pool marked HEALTHY at 02:35:12, routing restored.
Priya R.: ACME confirms latency back to normal at 02:38 UTC.
Jason K.: sorry — my change should have been limited canary. I'll add stricter rollout and update runbook.
Erin L.: add a unit test that simulates slow backend + short probe -> ensure no global failover unless threshold crossed.
Dave (SRE): captured tcpdump and envoy logs; attaching to ticket. key snippet: SNI on fallback traffic is correct, but remote peering path increased RTT.
Priya R.: writing up root cause: aggressive health timeout caused premature pool failover to backup region via peering, resulting in cross-region latency spike for some customers. mitigation: rollback timeout, change canary policy, add alert for cross-region routing changes.
Maya S.: also adding a dashboard: per-customer percent of traffic served outside preferred region.
Jason K.: created PR: revert-and-add-canary-guard (link: https://git.internal/r/1234).
Priya R.: closing loop with ACME, documenting repro and runbook steps in support ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
